findings_fixed: Global cross-model scratch alias: explicit namespace/TP-rank owner, independent standalone default owners.
Different captures on same stream alias: include capture sequence in workspace key and separate eager key.
External-launch raw-pointer lifetime: process-lifetime capture pins retain runtime, sidecars, scratch and input tensors.
Python/ctypes host enqueue interleaving: nonblocking per-owner lock rejects concurrent and reentrant calls before any stage.
DBO false does not imply no microbatching: check actual vLLM enable_dbo and use_ubatching before carrier construction.
Readiness canonicalization mismatch: reject noncanonical layer syntax instead of rewriting silently.
Traceback-reporting failure could bypass os._exit: BaseException catch plus finally guarantees status 78.
restrictions: No CUDA device launch or graph capture/replay occurred in this audit.
Captured resources are intentionally retained until worker exit. Repeated recapture grows retained memory.
Second construction of the same model namespace/layer/rank is rejected; reload requires a new worker.
DBO and microbatching unsupported. Separate namespaces and streams are structurally isolated, not device-concurrency qualified.
One host capture-state query and enqueue guard added; cost and production peak memory are unmeasured.
Device closure, real serving output, graph replay, determinism, KLD and TP4 throughput remain unqualified.
